arxiv-1404-6705.title: Singlet extension of the MSSM as a solution to the small cosmological scale anomalies
arxiv-1404-6705.creator: Fei Wang 1 , Wenyu Wang 2 , Jin Min Yang 3 , Sihong Zhou 2
arxiv-1404-6705.description: A 2014 arXiv research paper by Fei Wang 1 , Wenyu Wang 2 , Jin Min Yang 3 , Sihong Zhou 2. In this work we show that the general singlet extension of the MSSM can naturally provide a self-interacting singlino dark matter to solve the small cosmological scale anomalies (a large Sommerfeld enhancement factor can also be obtained). However, we find that the NMSSM (the singlet extension of the MSSM with Z 3 Z_{3} symmetry) cannot achieve this due to the restricted parameter space.

arxiv-2110-05365.title: Intriguing Properties of Input-Dependent Randomized Smoothing
arxiv-2110-05365.creator: Peter Súkeník, Aleksei Kuvshinov, Stephan Günnemann
arxiv-2110-05365.description: Abstract Randomized smoothing is currently considered the state-of-the-art method to obtain certifiably robust classifiers. Despite its remarkable performance, the method is associated with various serious problems such as “certified accuracy waterfalls”, certification vs. accuracy trade-off, or even fairness issues. Input-dependent smoothing approaches have been proposed with intention of overcoming these flaws.

arxiv-2304-11646.title: Rough Paths above Weierstrass Functions
arxiv-2304-11646.creator: \firstname Francesco \lastname Cellarosi, \firstname Zachary \lastname Selk
arxiv-2304-11646.description: Abstract Résumé. Rough paths theory allows for a pathwise theory of solutions to differential equations driven by highly irregular signals. The fundamental observation of rough paths theory is that if one can define “iterated integrals" above a signal, then one can construct solutions to differential equations driven by the signal.

arxiv-2404-14871.title: Exploring Human-AI Collaboration in Agile: Customised LLM Meeting Assistants
arxiv-2404-14871.creator: Beatriz Cabrero-Daniel 1, Tomas Herda 2, Victoria Pichler 2, Martin Eder 2
arxiv-2404-14871.description: Abstract This action research study focuses on the integration of “AI assistants” in two Agile software development meetings: the Daily Scrum and a feature refinement, a planning meeting that is part of an in-house Scaled Agile framework. We discuss the critical drivers of success, and establish a link between the use of AI and team collaboration dynamics.

arxiv-2407-21458.title: Shockwave-Enhanced Floquet Engineering in Relativistic Quasiparticles
arxiv-2407-21458.creator: Takashi Oka
arxiv-2407-21458.description: Abstract We investigate Floquet engineering of three-dimensional Dirac fermions driven by propagating waves, identifying distinct quantum states and phase transitions in the time-like, light-like, and space-like regimes. Notably, we uncover a novel regime where Floquet Weyl bands emerge and transition into Type-II Weyl states as the wave speed nears the Fermi velocity.

arxiv-2411-08832.title: Offline Adaptation of Quadruped Locomotion using Diffusion Models
arxiv-2411-08832.creator: Reece O’Mahoney, Alexander L. Mitchell, Wanming Yu, Ingmar Posner, Ioannis Havoutis
arxiv-2411-08832.description: Abstract We present a diffusion-based approach to quadrupedal locomotion that simultaneously addresses the limitations of learning and interpolating between multiple skills (modes) and of offline adapting to new locomotion behaviours after training. This is the first framework to apply classifier-free guided diffusion to quadruped locomotion and demonstrate its efficacy by extracting goal-conditioned behaviour from an originally unlabelled dataset.

arxiv-2506-19321.title: From kinetic mixtures to compressible two-phase flow: A BGK-type model and rigorous derivation
arxiv-2506-19321.creator: Seung Yeon Cho, Young-Pil Choi, Byung-Hoon Hwang, Sihyun Song
arxiv-2506-19321.description: Abstract . We propose a BGK-type kinetic model for a binary gas mixture, designed to serve as a kinetic formulation of compressible two-phase fluid dynamics. The model features species-dependent adiabatic exponents, and the relaxation operator is constructed by solving an entropy minimization problem under moments constraints.

arxiv-2511-10032.title: Moral Change or Noise? On Problems of Aligning AI With Temporally Unstable Human Feedback
arxiv-2511-10032.creator: Vijay Keswani, Cyrus Cousins, Breanna Nguyen, Vincent Conitzer ∗, Hoda Heidari ∗, Jana Schaich Borg ∗, Walter Sinnott-Armstrong ∗
arxiv-2511-10032.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Vijay Keswani, Cyrus Cousins, Breanna Nguyen, Vincent Conitzer ∗, Hoda Heidari ∗, Jana Schaich Borg ∗, Walter Sinnott-Armstrong ∗. Alignment methods in moral domains seek to elicit moral preferences of human stakeholders and incorporate them into AI. This presupposes moral preferences as static targets, but such preferences often evolve over time. Proper alignment of AI to dynamic human preferences should ideally account for “legitimate” changes to moral reasoning, while ignoring changes related to attention deficits, cognitive biases, or other arbitrary factors.

pmc-11323622.title: Experiences of intensive treatment for people with eating disorders: a systematic review and thematic synthesis
pmc-11323622.creator: Hannah Webb, Maria Griffiths, Ulrike Schmidt
pmc-11323622.description: BackgroundEating disorders are complex difficulties that impact the individual, their supporters and society. Increasing numbers are being admitted to intensive treatment settings (e.g., for inpatient treatment, day-patient treatment or acute medical treatment). The lived experience perspectives of what helps and hinders eating disorder recovery during intensive treatment is an emerging area of interest.

pmc-12418666.title: Understanding the complexities of oral healthcare delivery in correctional settings: a qualitative exploration of barriers, facilitators, and opportunities
pmc-12418666.creator: Arianna Amaya, Ivan Medina, Farimah Rezaei, Pegah Soleimani, Rebecca Bosworth, Heino Stöver, Babak Moazen
pmc-12418666.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). BackgroundPeople living in prison face exceptionally high prevalence rates of tooth decay, periodontal disease, and poor oral health-related quality of life. Despite its importance, various aspects of oral healthcare in prison settings remain understudied.

pmc-12461679.title: Hyperpolarized NMR Combined with Quantum Mechanical Simulations Reveal Atomistic Structures of Calcium Phosphate Prenucleation Clusters
pmc-12461679.creator: Christopher Pötzl, Ertan Turhan, Christel Gervais, Thierry Azaïs, Dennis Kurzbach
pmc-12461679.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). The discovery of solute precursors of crystalline materials, such as biominerals, recently challenged the classical nucleation theory (CNT). One emerging method for investigating these early-stage intermediates in solution is dissolution dynamic nuclear polarization (dDNP)-enhanced nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) spectroscopy. Recent applications of dDNP to calcium carbonate (CaC) and calcium phosphate (CaP) mineralization have demonstrated the feasibility of identifying and tracing very early-stage prenucleation clusters (PNCs).

pmc-12469837.title: Assessing the Impact of Computable Type 2 Diabetes Phenotypes on Predicting Healthcare Utilization Using Electronic Health Records and Administrative Claims
pmc-12469837.creator: Priyanka D. Sood, Star Liu, Chintan Pandya, Hadi Kharrazi
pmc-12469837.description: Background/Objectives: Type 2 Diabetes (T2D) computable phenotypes, which leverage electronic health records (EHRs) and administrative claims data, provide the basis for T2D population health research. Our study investigates how T2D phenotypes affect downstream healthcare utilization prediction, specifically inpatient (IP) and emergency room (ER) admissions.

pmc-12627525.title: CD38-specific nanobody-based bispecific antibody recruiters (BARs) redirect complement-dependent cytotoxicity toward multiple myeloma cells
pmc-12627525.creator: Luca Julius Pape, Anna Josephine Gebhardt, Marten Dannenberg, Henry Risch, Anya Duttmann, Katja Weisel, Julia Hambach, Friedrich Koch-Nolte, Peter Bannas
pmc-12627525.description: Bispecific antibody recruiters (BARs) are an innovative class of immunotherapeutics that redirect endogenous antibodies to tumor cells. BARs comprise a tumor-binding and an antibody-binding module, enabling endogenous antibodies to opsonize tumor cells and induce FC-dependent effector functions such as complement-dependent cytotoxicity (CDC).

pmc-13457639.title: CRIT AI 4.0: A Locally Deployable Artificial Intelligence System for Mortality Risk Stratification and Clinical Decision Support in Intensive Care Units
pmc-13457639.creator: Pratik Kumar Mitra
pmc-13457639.description: Background and aimsIntensive care unit (ICU) mortality in India remains high, with risk stratification inconsistently applied in resource-limited settings where AI-based decision support requires cloud connectivity unavailable to most Indian hospitals. We describe CRIT AI 4.0, a proof-of-concept, locally deployable, offline-capable AI-assisted decision support system for resource-constrained Indian ICUs.Patients and methodsA Python-based Windows application was developed, operating fully offline.

pmc-13712282.title: Ultra-sensitive detection of receptor binding domain of SARS-CoV-2 based on artificial intelligence assisted antibody selection and antibody‒nucleic acid conjugation signal amplification
pmc-13712282.creator: Jiatong Liu, Wenfan Chen, Xiufeng Li, Yuanyuan Luo, Qiaomin Li, Wenbin Zhao, Qiaojun He, Su Zeng, Zhan Zhou, Sheng Cai
pmc-13712282.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). The emergence of SARS-CoV-2 has led to a global pandemic, causing unprecedented disruption to health systems and economies worldwide, calling for an urgent imperative for precise and sensitive diagnostic method. To address this, a novel detection method, termed antibody‒nucleic acid conjugate linked immunosorbent assay (ANCLISA), was designed for the ultra-sensitive detection of the receptor binding domain (RBD) of SARS-CoV-2, which play a pivotal role in the diagnosis of COVID-19.
